name: Lion
diet: large herbivores such as zebra and wildebeest (carnivore)
fun_fact: The only big cat that lives in social groups, called prides.
description: Lion (Panthera leo) is a mammal that lives in open savanna and grassland, found in sub-Saharan Africa. Diet: large herbivores such as zebra and wildebeest (carnivore). Conservation status: Vulnerable. The only big cat that lives in social groups, called prides.

name: Tiger
region: South and Southeast Asia, Russian Far East
diet: deer, wild boar, and other large mammals (carnivore)
fun_fact: Each tiger has a unique stripe pattern, like a fingerprint.
description: Tiger (Panthera tigris) is a mammal that lives in forests, mangroves, and grasslands, found in South and Southeast Asia, Russian Far East. Diet: deer, wild boar, and other large mammals (carnivore). Conservation status: Endangered. Each tiger has a unique stripe pattern, like a fingerprint.

name: African Elephant
fun_fact: The largest living land animal; a trunk has over 40,000 muscles.
description: African Elephant (Loxodonta africana) is a mammal that lives in savanna, forest, and desert, found in sub-Saharan Africa. Diet: grasses, bark, roots, and fruit (herbivore). Conservation status: Endangered. The largest living land animal; a trunk has over 40,000 muscles.

name: Asian Elephant
fun_fact: Smaller ears than its African cousin and only some males grow tusks.
description: Asian Elephant (Elephas maximus) is a mammal that lives in tropical forest and grassland, found in South and Southeast Asia. Diet: grasses, bark, and fruit (herbivore). Conservation status: Endangered. Smaller ears than its African cousin and only some males grow tusks.

name: Giraffe
fun_fact: The tallest living land animal, with a neck too short to have extra vertebrae - it has the same seven neck bones as a human.
description: Giraffe (Giraffa camelopardalis) is a mammal that lives in savanna and open woodland, found in sub-Saharan Africa. Diet: acacia leaves and shoots (herbivore). Conservation status: Vulnerable. The tallest living land animal, with a neck too short to have extra vertebrae - it has the same seven neck bones as a human.

name: Plains Zebra
fun_fact: No two zebras have the exact same stripe pattern.
description: Plains Zebra (Equus quagga) is a mammal that lives in grassland and savanna, found in eastern and southern Africa. Diet: grasses (herbivore). Conservation status: Near Threatened. No two zebras have the exact same stripe pattern.

name: Hippopotamus
fun_fact: Despite its bulk, a hippo can outrun a human on land over short distances.
description: Hippopotamus (Hippopotamus amphibius) is a mammal that lives in rivers and lakes, found in sub-Saharan Africa. Diet: grasses (herbivore). Conservation status: Vulnerable. Despite its bulk, a hippo can outrun a human on land over short distances.

name: White Rhinoceros
fun_fact: The wide, square lip is built for grazing on grass, unlike the black rhino's pointed lip.
description: White Rhinoceros (Ceratotherium simum) is a mammal that lives in grassland and savanna, found in southern Africa. Diet: grasses (herbivore). Conservation status: Near Threatened. The wide, square lip is built for grazing on grass, unlike the black rhino's pointed lip.

name: Black Rhinoceros
fun_fact: Uses its hooked upper lip to strip leaves from bushes.
description: Black Rhinoceros (Diceros bicornis) is a mammal that lives in savanna and shrubland, found in eastern and southern Africa. Diet: leaves and shrubs (browser/herbivore). Conservation status: Critically Endangered. Uses its hooked upper lip to strip leaves from bushes.

name: Western Lowland Gorilla
fun_fact: Shares about 98% of its DNA with humans.
description: Western Lowland Gorilla (Gorilla gorilla gorilla) is a mammal that lives in tropical rainforest, found in Central Africa. Diet: fruit, leaves, and stems (herbivore). Conservation status: Critically Endangered. Shares about 98% of its DNA with humans.

name: Chimpanzee
fun_fact: Known to use tools, such as stripped twigs to fish for termites.
description: Chimpanzee (Pan troglodytes) is a mammal that lives in tropical forest and savanna woodland, found in Central and West Africa. Diet: fruit, leaves, and insects (omnivore). Conservation status: Endangered. Known to use tools, such as stripped twigs to fish for termites.

name: Bornean Orangutan
fun_fact: Spends most of its life in trees and builds a fresh sleeping nest every night.
description: Bornean Orangutan (Pongo pygmaeus) is a mammal that lives in tropical rainforest, found in Borneo. Diet: fruit, bark, and leaves (omnivore). Conservation status: Critically Endangered. Spends most of its life in trees and builds a fresh sleeping nest every night.

name: Red Kangaroo
fun_fact: Can cover over 8 meters in a single hop.
description: Red Kangaroo (Osphranter rufus) is a mammal that lives in arid plains and open woodland, found in Australia. Diet: grasses and shrubs (herbivore). Conservation status: Least Concern. Can cover over 8 meters in a single hop.

name: Koala
fun_fact: Sleeps up to 20 hours a day to conserve energy from its low-nutrient diet.
description: Koala (Phascolarctos cinereus) is a mammal that lives in eucalyptus forest, found in eastern Australia. Diet: eucalyptus leaves (herbivore). Conservation status: Vulnerable. Sleeps up to 20 hours a day to conserve energy from its low-nutrient diet.

name: Giant Panda
fun_fact: Eats up to 40 kg of bamboo a day despite having a carnivore's digestive system.
description: Giant Panda (Ailuropoda melanoleuca) is a mammal that lives in temperate bamboo forest, found in central China. Diet: bamboo, almost exclusively (herbivore). Conservation status: Vulnerable. Eats up to 40 kg of bamboo a day despite having a carnivore's digestive system.

name: Red Panda
fun_fact: Not closely related to the giant panda; it's the only living member of its own family.
description: Red Panda (Ailurus fulgens) is a mammal that lives in temperate forest with bamboo understory, found in Himalayas and southwestern China. Diet: bamboo, fruit, and insects (omnivore). Conservation status: Endangered. Not closely related to the giant panda; it's the only living member of its own family.

name: Polar Bear
fun_fact: Black skin under a translucent, hollow-haired coat helps absorb heat from the sun.
description: Polar Bear (Ursus maritimus) is a mammal that lives in arctic sea ice and coastline, found in the Arctic. Diet: seals (carnivore). Conservation status: Vulnerable. Black skin under a translucent, hollow-haired coat helps absorb heat from the sun.

name: Grizzly Bear
diet: berries, roots, fish, and small mammals (omnivore)
fun_fact: Has a distinctive shoulder hump made of muscle for digging.
description: Grizzly Bear (Ursus arctos horribilis) is a mammal that lives in forest, mountain, and tundra, found in North America. Diet: berries, roots, fish, and small mammals (omnivore). Conservation status: Least Concern. Has a distinctive shoulder hump made of muscle for digging.

name: Gray Wolf
diet: deer, elk, and other large prey (carnivore)
fun_fact: Lives and hunts in family groups called packs, led by a breeding pair.
description: Gray Wolf (Canis lupus) is a mammal that lives in forest, tundra, and grassland, found in North America, Europe, and Asia. Diet: deer, elk, and other large prey (carnivore). Conservation status: Least Concern. Lives and hunts in family groups called packs, led by a breeding pair.

name: Red Fox
fun_fact: The most widely distributed wild carnivore on Earth.
description: Red Fox (Vulpes vulpes) is a mammal that lives in forest, grassland, and urban edges, found in widespread across the Northern Hemisphere. Diet: small mammals, birds, and fruit (omnivore). Conservation status: Least Concern. The most widely distributed wild carnivore on Earth.

name: Fennec Fox
fun_fact: Its oversized ears radiate heat and help it hear prey underground.
description: Fennec Fox (Vulpes zerda) is a mammal that lives in sandy desert, found in North Africa and the Sahara. Diet: insects, small rodents, and plants (omnivore). Conservation status: Least Concern. Its oversized ears radiate heat and help it hear prey underground.

name: Meerkat
fun_fact: Lives in tight-knit mobs and posts sentries to watch for predators.
description: Meerkat (Suricata suricatta) is a mammal that lives in arid grassland and desert, found in southern Africa. Diet: insects and small reptiles (omnivore). Conservation status: Least Concern. Lives in tight-knit mobs and posts sentries to watch for predators.

name: Spotted Hyena
fun_fact: Has one of the strongest bites in the animal kingdom, able to crack bone.
description: Spotted Hyena (Crocuta crocuta) is a mammal that lives in savanna and grassland, found in sub-Saharan Africa. Diet: large mammals, hunted or scavenged (carnivore). Conservation status: Least Concern. Has one of the strongest bites in the animal kingdom, able to crack bone.

name: Cheetah
fun_fact: The fastest land animal, capable of short bursts near 100 km/h.
description: Cheetah (Acinonyx jubatus) is a mammal that lives in open savanna and grassland, found in sub-Saharan Africa. Diet: small to medium antelope (carnivore). Conservation status: Vulnerable. The fastest land animal, capable of short bursts near 100 km/h.

name: Leopard
fun_fact: Often hauls its kills up into trees to keep them from other predators.
description: Leopard (Panthera pardus) is a mammal that lives in forest, savanna, and mountains, found in Africa and Asia. Diet: a wide variety of prey (carnivore). Conservation status: Vulnerable. Often hauls its kills up into trees to keep them from other predators.

name: Jaguar
fun_fact: Has the strongest bite force relative to size of any big cat.
description: Jaguar (Panthera onca) is a mammal that lives in tropical rainforest and wetland, found in Central and South America. Diet: capybara, caiman, and fish (carnivore). Conservation status: Near Threatened. Has the strongest bite force relative to size of any big cat.

name: Ocelot
fun_fact: A skilled climber and swimmer, mostly active at night.
description: Ocelot (Leopardus pardalis) is a mammal that lives in dense forest and scrubland, found in Central and South America. Diet: small mammals and birds (carnivore). Conservation status: Least Concern. A skilled climber and swimmer, mostly active at night.

name: River Otter
fun_fact: Known for sliding down muddy or snowy banks, seemingly for play.
description: River Otter (Lontra canadensis) is a mammal that lives in rivers, lakes, and coastlines, found in North America. Diet: fish and crustaceans (carnivore). Conservation status: Least Concern. Known for sliding down muddy or snowy banks, seemingly for play.

name: American Beaver
fun_fact: Builds dams and lodges that can reshape entire wetland ecosystems.
description: American Beaver (Castor canadensis) is a mammal that lives in rivers, streams, and wetlands, found in North America. Diet: bark, twigs, and aquatic plants (herbivore). Conservation status: Least Concern. Builds dams and lodges that can reshape entire wetland ecosystems.

name: Raccoon
fun_fact: Has highly sensitive front paws it uses to examine food and objects.
description: Raccoon (Procyon lotor) is a mammal that lives in forest, wetland, and urban areas, found in North America. Diet: fruit, insects, and small animals (omnivore). Conservation status: Least Concern. Has highly sensitive front paws it uses to examine food and objects.

name: Striped Skunk
fun_fact: Defends itself with a strong-smelling spray from glands near its tail.
description: Striped Skunk (Mephitis mephitis) is a mammal that lives in woodland, grassland, and suburbs, found in North America. Diet: insects, small rodents, and plants (omnivore). Conservation status: Least Concern. Defends itself with a strong-smelling spray from glands near its tail.

name: Nine-banded Armadillo
fun_fact: Almost always gives birth to identical quadruplets.
description: Nine-banded Armadillo (Dasypus novemcinctus) is a mammal that lives in grassland, forest, and scrub, found in the Americas. Diet: insects, especially ants and termites (insectivore). Conservation status: Least Concern. Almost always gives birth to identical quadruplets.

name: Giant Anteater
fun_fact: Its tongue can flick in and out up to 150 times a minute.
description: Giant Anteater (Myrmecophaga tridactyla) is a mammal that lives in grassland and open forest, found in Central and South America. Diet: ants and termites (insectivore). Conservation status: Vulnerable. Its tongue can flick in and out up to 150 times a minute.

name: Three-toed Sloth
fun_fact: Moves so slowly that algae often grows in its fur.
description: Three-toed Sloth (Bradypus variegatus) is a mammal that lives in tropical rainforest canopy, found in Central and South America. Diet: leaves (herbivore). Conservation status: Least Concern. Moves so slowly that algae often grows in its fur.

name: Capybara
fun_fact: The world's largest living rodent, and a strong swimmer.
description: Capybara (Hydrochoerus hydrochaeris) is a mammal that lives in wetland, riverbank, and grassland, found in South America. Diet: grasses and aquatic plants (herbivore). Conservation status: Least Concern. The world's largest living rodent, and a strong swimmer.

name: Bactrian Camel
fun_fact: Its two humps store fat, not water, for long treks between food sources.
description: Bactrian Camel (Camelus bactrianus) is a mammal that lives in cold desert and steppe, found in Central Asia. Diet: tough desert vegetation (herbivore). Conservation status: Endangered. Its two humps store fat, not water, for long treks between food sources.

name: Llama
fun_fact: Domesticated for thousands of years as a pack animal and wool source.
description: Llama (Lama glama) is a mammal that lives in high-altitude grassland, found in the Andes mountains. Diet: grasses (herbivore). Conservation status: Least Concern. Domesticated for thousands of years as a pack animal and wool source.

name: Alpaca
fun_fact: Bred mainly for its soft, warm fleece rather than as a pack animal.
description: Alpaca (Vicugna pacos) is a mammal that lives in high-altitude grassland, found in the Andes mountains. Diet: grasses (herbivore). Conservation status: Least Concern. Bred mainly for its soft, warm fleece rather than as a pack animal.

name: American Bison
fun_fact: Once nearly extinct, but conservation efforts have rebuilt herds across the continent.
description: American Bison (Bison bison) is a mammal that lives in prairie and grassland, found in North America. Diet: grasses (herbivore). Conservation status: Near Threatened. Once nearly extinct, but conservation efforts have rebuilt herds across the continent.

name: Moose
fun_fact: The largest living species of deer.
description: Moose (Alces alces) is a mammal that lives in boreal forest and wetland, found in North America, Europe, and Asia. Diet: leaves, bark, and aquatic plants (herbivore). Conservation status: Least Concern. The largest living species of deer.

name: Reindeer
fun_fact: The only deer species where both males and females grow antlers.
description: Reindeer (Rangifer tarandus) is a mammal that lives in tundra and boreal forest, found in the Arctic and sub-Arctic. Diet: lichen, grasses, and leaves (herbivore). Conservation status: Vulnerable. The only deer species where both males and females grow antlers.

name: Hedgehog
fun_fact: Rolls into a tight, spiny ball when threatened.
description: Hedgehog (Erinaceus europaeus) is a mammal that lives in woodland, grassland, and gardens, found in Europe. Diet: insects, worms, and small invertebrates (insectivore). Conservation status: Least Concern. Rolls into a tight, spiny ball when threatened.

name: Platypus
fun_fact: One of the only mammals that lays eggs, and males have a venomous spur.
description: Platypus (Ornithorhynchus anatinus) is a mammal that lives in rivers and streams, found in eastern Australia. Diet: insect larvae, shrimp, and worms (carnivore). Conservation status: Near Threatened. One of the only mammals that lays eggs, and males have a venomous spur.

name: Short-beaked Echidna
fun_fact: Along with the platypus, one of the only egg-laying mammals on Earth.
description: Short-beaked Echidna (Tachyglossus aculeatus) is a mammal that lives in forest, scrubland, and desert, found in Australia and New Guinea. Diet: ants and termites (insectivore). Conservation status: Least Concern. Along with the platypus, one of the only egg-laying mammals on Earth.

name: Common Wombat
fun_fact: Produces cube-shaped droppings, which help mark territory without rolling away.
description: Common Wombat (Vombatus ursinus) is a mammal that lives in forest and grassland, found in southeastern Australia. Diet: grasses and roots (herbivore). Conservation status: Least Concern. Produces cube-shaped droppings, which help mark territory without rolling away.

name: Tasmanian Devil
fun_fact: The largest carnivorous marsupial alive today, known for its powerful bite.
description: Tasmanian Devil (Sarcophilus harrisii) is a mammal that lives in forest and coastal scrubland, found in Tasmania, Australia. Diet: carrion and small animals (carnivore/scavenger). Conservation status: Endangered. The largest carnivorous marsupial alive today, known for its powerful bite.

name: Warthog
fun_fact: Often backs into burrows so its tusks face outward toward danger.
description: Warthog (Phacochoerus africanus) is a mammal that lives in savanna and grassland, found in sub-Saharan Africa. Diet: grasses and roots (herbivore). Conservation status: Least Concern. Often backs into burrows so its tusks face outward toward danger.

name: Okapi
fun_fact: Striped legs resemble a zebra, but it's actually the giraffe's closest living relative.
description: Okapi (Okapia johnstoni) is a mammal that lives in dense tropical rainforest, found in Democratic Republic of the Congo. Diet: leaves and shoots (herbivore). Conservation status: Endangered. Striped legs resemble a zebra, but it's actually the giraffe's closest living relative.

name: Aardvark
fun_fact: Digs burrows so efficiently it can disappear into the ground in minutes.
description: Aardvark (Orycteropus afer) is a mammal that lives in savanna and grassland, found in sub-Saharan Africa. Diet: ants and termites (insectivore). Conservation status: Least Concern. Digs burrows so efficiently it can disappear into the ground in minutes.

name: Pangolin
fun_fact: The only mammal covered in protective keratin scales.
description: Pangolin (Manis species) is a mammal that lives in forest and savanna, found in Africa and Asia. Diet: ants and termites (insectivore). Conservation status: Critically Endangered. The only mammal covered in protective keratin scales.

name: Emperor Penguin
fun_fact: The largest penguin species; males incubate the egg on their feet through the Antarctic winter.
description: Emperor Penguin (Aptenodytes forsteri) is a bird that lives in sea ice and open ocean, found in Antarctica. Diet: fish, squid, and krill (carnivore). Conservation status: Near Threatened. The largest penguin species; males incubate the egg on their feet through the Antarctic winter.

name: King Penguin
fun_fact: The second-largest penguin species, with a distinctive orange neck patch.
description: King Penguin (Aptenodytes patagonicus) is a bird that lives in sub-Antarctic islands and ocean, found in southern Atlantic and Indian Oceans. Diet: fish and squid (carnivore). Conservation status: Least Concern. The second-largest penguin species, with a distinctive orange neck patch.

name: Humboldt Penguin
fun_fact: One of the warm-climate penguin species, found far from Antarctica.
description: Humboldt Penguin (Spheniscus humboldti) is a bird that lives in rocky coastline, found in coasts of Chile and Peru. Diet: fish, especially anchovies (carnivore). Conservation status: Vulnerable. One of the warm-climate penguin species, found far from Antarctica.

name: Bald Eagle
fun_fact: Builds some of the largest tree nests of any bird, reused and expanded yearly.
description: Bald Eagle (Haliaeetus leucocephalus) is a bird that lives in lakes, rivers, and coastlines, found in North America. Diet: fish and small mammals (carnivore). Conservation status: Least Concern. Builds some of the largest tree nests of any bird, reused and expanded yearly.

name: Golden Eagle
fun_fact: One of the fastest diving birds, reaching speeds over 240 km/h in a stoop.
description: Golden Eagle (Aquila chrysaetos) is a bird that lives in mountains and open country, found in Northern Hemisphere. Diet: rabbits and other small mammals (carnivore). Conservation status: Least Concern. One of the fastest diving birds, reaching speeds over 240 km/h in a stoop.

name: Snowy Owl
fun_fact: Unlike most owls, it often hunts during daylight in the Arctic summer.
description: Snowy Owl (Bubo scandiacus) is a bird that lives in arctic tundra, found in the Arctic. Diet: lemmings and other small mammals (carnivore). Conservation status: Vulnerable. Unlike most owls, it often hunts during daylight in the Arctic summer.

name: Great Horned Owl
fun_fact: Silent flight feathers let it approach prey almost without a sound.
description: Great Horned Owl (Bubo virginianus) is a bird that lives in forest, desert, and urban edges, found in the Americas. Diet: small mammals and birds (carnivore). Conservation status: Least Concern. Silent flight feathers let it approach prey almost without a sound.

name: Scarlet Macaw
fun_fact: Can live 50 years or more and often mates for life.
description: Scarlet Macaw (Ara macao) is a bird that lives in tropical rainforest, found in Central and South America. Diet: fruit, nuts, and seeds (herbivore). Conservation status: Least Concern. Can live 50 years or more and often mates for life.

name: African Grey Parrot
fun_fact: Considered one of the most vocally talented and cognitively advanced parrots.
description: African Grey Parrot (Psittacus erithacus) is a bird that lives in tropical rainforest, found in West and Central Africa. Diet: fruit, seeds, and nuts (herbivore). Conservation status: Endangered. Considered one of the most vocally talented and cognitively advanced parrots.

name: Toco Toucan
fun_fact: Its oversized bill helps regulate body temperature by releasing heat.
description: Toco Toucan (Ramphastos toco) is a bird that lives in tropical forest and savanna, found in South America. Diet: fruit and small animals (omnivore). Conservation status: Least Concern. Its oversized bill helps regulate body temperature by releasing heat.

name: Greater Flamingo
fun_fact: Its pink color comes from pigments in the algae and shrimp it eats.
description: Greater Flamingo (Phoenicopterus roseus) is a bird that lives in shallow lakes and lagoons, found in Africa, southern Europe, and Asia. Diet: algae and small crustaceans (omnivore/filter feeder). Conservation status: Least Concern. Its pink color comes from pigments in the algae and shrimp it eats.

name: Common Ostrich
fun_fact: The largest living bird; it cannot fly but can sprint over 70 km/h.
description: Common Ostrich (Struthio camelus) is a bird that lives in savanna and desert, found in Africa. Diet: plants, seeds, and small animals (omnivore). Conservation status: Least Concern. The largest living bird; it cannot fly but can sprint over 70 km/h.

name: Emu
fun_fact: The second-largest living bird by height, after the ostrich.
description: Emu (Dromaius novaehollandiae) is a bird that lives in grassland and open woodland, found in Australia. Diet: plants, seeds, and insects (omnivore). Conservation status: Least Concern. The second-largest living bird by height, after the ostrich.

name: Southern Cassowary
fun_fact: A bony helmet-like casque tops its head; considered one of the more dangerous birds.
description: Southern Cassowary (Casuarius casuarius) is a bird that lives in tropical rainforest, found in Australia and New Guinea. Diet: fallen fruit (frugivore). Conservation status: Least Concern. A bony helmet-like casque tops its head; considered one of the more dangerous birds.

name: Indian Peafowl
fun_fact: Males, called peacocks, fan out iridescent tail feathers to attract mates.
description: Indian Peafowl (Pavo cristatus) is a bird that lives in forest edge and farmland, found in the Indian subcontinent. Diet: seeds, insects, and small reptiles (omnivore). Conservation status: Least Concern. Males, called peacocks, fan out iridescent tail feathers to attract mates.

name: American White Pelican
fun_fact: Often fishes cooperatively, herding fish into shallow water with other pelicans.
description: American White Pelican (Pelecanus erythrorhynchos) is a bird that lives in lakes and wetlands, found in North America. Diet: fish (carnivore). Conservation status: Least Concern. Often fishes cooperatively, herding fish into shallow water with other pelicans.

name: Whooping Crane
fun_fact: One of the rarest birds in North America; conservation programs use costume-clad handlers to teach chicks migration routes.
description: Whooping Crane (Grus americana) is a bird that lives in wetland and prairie marsh, found in North America. Diet: fish, insects, and plants (omnivore). Conservation status: Endangered. One of the rarest birds in North America; conservation programs use costume-clad handlers to teach chicks migration routes.

name: Trumpeter Swan
fun_fact: The heaviest native waterfowl in North America.
description: Trumpeter Swan (Cygnus buccinator) is a bird that lives in lakes, rivers, and wetlands, found in North America. Diet: aquatic plants (herbivore). Conservation status: Least Concern. The heaviest native waterfowl in North America.

name: Rufous Hummingbird
fun_fact: Makes one of the longest migratory journeys relative to body size of any bird.
description: Rufous Hummingbird (Selasphorus rufus) is a bird that lives in forest edge and gardens, found in western North America. Diet: nectar and small insects (nectarivore). Conservation status: Near Threatened. Makes one of the longest migratory journeys relative to body size of any bird.

name: Brown Kiwi
fun_fact: A flightless bird with nostrils at the tip of its beak, used to sniff out food underground.
description: Brown Kiwi (Apteryx mantelli) is a bird that lives in forest floor, found in New Zealand. Diet: insects, worms, and seeds (omnivore). Conservation status: Vulnerable. A flightless bird with nostrils at the tip of its beak, used to sniff out food underground.

name: American Alligator
fun_fact: A conservation success story, recovering from near extinction in the mid-20th century.
description: American Alligator (Alligator mississippiensis) is a reptile that lives in freshwater swamp, marsh, and river, found in southeastern United States. Diet: fish, birds, and mammals (carnivore). Conservation status: Least Concern. A conservation success story, recovering from near extinction in the mid-20th century.

name: Saltwater Crocodile
fun_fact: The largest living reptile, with adult males exceeding 6 meters.
description: Saltwater Crocodile (Crocodylus porosus) is a reptile that lives in coastal wetland and river estuary, found in Southeast Asia and northern Australia. Diet: fish, birds, and mammals (carnivore). Conservation status: Least Concern. The largest living reptile, with adult males exceeding 6 meters.

name: Komodo Dragon
region: the Indonesian islands of Komodo and Flores
fun_fact: The largest living lizard, with a bite that delivers venom and bacteria-laden saliva.
description: Komodo Dragon (Varanus komodoensis) is a reptile that lives in dry savanna and forest, found in the Indonesian islands of Komodo and Flores. Diet: deer, pigs, and carrion (carnivore). Conservation status: Endangered. The largest living lizard, with a bite that delivers venom and bacteria-laden saliva.

name: Green Iguana
fun_fact: Can drop its tail to escape a predator, then regrow it over time.
description: Green Iguana (Iguana iguana) is a reptile that lives in tropical rainforest canopy, found in Central and South America. Diet: leaves, flowers, and fruit (herbivore). Conservation status: Least Concern. Can drop its tail to escape a predator, then regrow it over time.

name: Veiled Chameleon
fun_fact: Its independently swiveling eyes give it a nearly 360-degree field of view.
description: Veiled Chameleon (Chamaeleo calyptratus) is a reptile that lives in mountain valleys and plateaus, found in Yemen and Saudi Arabia. Diet: insects and some plant matter (omnivore). Conservation status: Least Concern. Its independently swiveling eyes give it a nearly 360-degree field of view.

name: Leopard Gecko
region: South Asia and the Middle East
fun_fact: Unlike most geckos, it has movable eyelids and no adhesive toe pads.
description: Leopard Gecko (Eublepharis macularius) is a reptile that lives in rocky, arid grassland, found in South Asia and the Middle East. Diet: insects (insectivore). Conservation status: Least Concern. Unlike most geckos, it has movable eyelids and no adhesive toe pads.

name: Nile Monitor
fun_fact: One of Africa's largest lizards and a strong swimmer.
description: Nile Monitor (Varanus niloticus) is a reptile that lives in rivers, lakes, and wetlands, found in sub-Saharan Africa. Diet: eggs, fish, and small animals (carnivore). Conservation status: Least Concern. One of Africa's largest lizards and a strong swimmer.

name: Galapagos Tortoise
fun_fact: Among the longest-lived vertebrates, with some individuals surpassing 100 years.
description: Galapagos Tortoise (Chelonoidis niger) is a reptile that lives in volcanic scrubland and grassland, found in the Galapagos Islands. Diet: grasses, cactus, and fruit (herbivore). Conservation status: Vulnerable. Among the longest-lived vertebrates, with some individuals surpassing 100 years.

name: Green Sea Turtle
habitat: coastal waters, seagrass beds, and coral reefs
